correctness.rationale: The exact graph and incoming NOR rule are specified, with quantifiers q>=2 and d>=1. The prefix-collapse lemma reduces every orbit to the (q+1)-symbol loopless complete graph, where zero, one-hot and multi-hot vectors determine all fixed and primitive-two recurrence. The input-output disjoint q-ary tree partition proves the all-depth CDF and fixed basin counts. A monotonicity argument for the second iterate of f(p)=(1-p)^q excludes other interior attractors and gives the critical survival limit. Full finite enumerations and exact independent integer formulas agree for five instances; random tests on an additional graph are not invoked as proof of the infinite claim.

value.rationale: Kautz networks are a canonical sparse directed word topology, and the no-repeated-adjacent-symbol constraint creates new frozen one-hot phases absent in a full-word de Bruijn comparator. The all-depth exact entrance distribution, sharp maximal transient, uniform-input labelled counts, and isolated critical-bias survival answer motivated natural dynamical questions for every depth and alphabet. Neither a tiny finite census nor an isolated application of the NOR-tree recursion is the main claim.
